Pay within 10 days for a 2% discount
Pay within 2 days for a 10% discount
Pay at day 30 for a 2% discount
Get a 10% discount if paid within 2 days
Without the discount, the full amount is due within 30 days.

Inventory cost increases
It is a selling expense
Sales decrease
COGS decreases immediately

Dr COGS / Cr Inventory
Dr Inventory / Cr COGS
Dr Sales / Cr Cash
Nothing more
Cost of goods sold is recorded with every sale.

Gross profit =
Net sales − COGS
Net sales − Expenses
Sales + COGS
COGS − Sales
It is before operating expenses.

Which is excluded from the acid-test ratio?
Inventory
Cash
Short-term investments
Current receivables
Quick assets exclude inventory.
c5
Which of the following accounts is used under a perpetual inventory system but NOT under a periodic inventory system?
Cost of Goods Sold
Purchases
Purchase Returns and Allowances
Freight-In
Perpetual records Cost of Goods Sold with every sale. Purchases, Purchase Returns and Freight-In are periodic-system accounts (perpetual uses Inventory).
c5
Credit terms of 2/10, n/30 mean that:
A 2% discount is allowed if paid within 10 days; otherwise, the full amount is due in 30 days.
A 10% discount is allowed if paid within 2 days.
The invoice must be paid within 10 to 30 days.
A 2% penalty is charged after 10 days.
2/10, n/30 = 2% discount if paid within 10 days, otherwise the full amount is due in 30 days.
c5
Under FOB Shipping Point, who pays the freight costs and when does title pass?
Buyer pays; title passes at shipping point.
Seller pays; title passes at destination.
Seller pays; title passes at shipping point.
Buyer pays; title passes at destination.
FOB shipping point: title passes when the goods leave the seller, so the buyer owns them in transit and pays the freight.
c5
Gross Profit is calculated as:
Net Sales minus Cost of Goods Sold
Net Sales minus Operating Expenses
Sales Revenue minus Sales Discounts
Cost of Goods Sold minus Operating Expenses
Gross profit = net sales − cost of goods sold.
c5

A company sells merchandise for $10,000 on account with terms 1/10, n/30. The customer returns $2,000 of merchandise and pays the balance within the discount period. What is the amount of cash received?
Net sales on the invoice = 10,000 − 2,000 = 8,000. Discount 1% × 8,000 = 80, so cash = 8,000 − 80 = 7,920.
c5
Which of the following is a contra-revenue account?
Sales Returns and Allowances
Cost of Goods Sold
Purchase Discounts
Freight-Out
Sales Returns and Allowances is deducted from sales revenue, so it is contra-revenue. Purchase Discounts is a contra-purchases/inventory account.
c5
In a perpetual inventory system, a return of defective merchandise by a purchaser is recorded by crediting:
Inventory
Purchases
Purchase Returns and Allowances
Cost of Goods Sold
Perpetual system: the buyer credits Inventory for returned goods (periodic would credit Purchase Returns and Allowances).
c5
Freight-Out is classified on a multiple-step income statement as:
An Operating Expense
Cost of Goods Sold
A Contra-Revenue
Other Expenses and Losses
Freight-out is the seller's delivery cost, an operating (selling) expense, not part of COGS.
c5
If Beginning Inventory is $40,000, Cost of Goods Purchased is $250,000, and Ending Inventory is $50,000, what is Cost of Goods Sold?
c5
Which entry is required when a company sells goods on account under a perpetual system?
Debit Accounts Receivable, Credit Sales; AND Debit Cost of Goods Sold, Credit Inventory.
Debit Accounts Receivable, Credit Sales only.
Debit Inventory, Credit Cost of Goods Sold.
Debit Sales, Credit Accounts Receivable.
Perpetual: record the sale (Dr Accounts Receivable, Cr Sales) and the cost (Dr COGS, Cr Inventory) at the same time.
c5
Net Sales equals Sales Revenue minus:
Sales Returns and Allowances and Sales Discounts
Cost of Goods Sold
Operating Expenses
Freight-In
Net sales = sales revenue − sales returns and allowances − sales discounts.
c5
The operating cycle of a merchandising company is ordinarily:
Longer than that of a service company.
Shorter than that of a service company.
Exactly one year.
Equal to the fiscal year.
A merchandiser must buy and sell goods, so its cycle (cash → inventory → receivables → cash) is longer than a service company's.
c5
An income statement that shows several steps in determining net income is called a:
Multiple-step income statement
Single-step income statement
Classified income statement
Condensed income statement
A multiple-step income statement shows gross profit and income from operations on the way to net income.
c5
Gross Profit Rate is computed by dividing Gross Profit by:
Net Sales
Total Assets
Cost of Goods Sold
Net Income
Gross profit rate = gross profit ÷ net sales.
c5
Under a periodic inventory system, Cost of Goods Sold is determined:
At the end of the accounting period.
After each sale.
Daily.
Whenever inventory is purchased.
Periodic: COGS is worked out at the end of the period from the physical count (BI + purchases − EI).
c5
Which of the following is NOT included in Cost of Goods Purchased?
Freight-Out
Purchases
Freight-In
Purchase Discounts
Freight-out is a selling expense. Cost of goods purchased includes purchases, freight-in, and is reduced by returns and discounts.
c5
A physical count of inventory is necessary under a perpetual system to:
Check the accuracy of perpetual records and detect shrinkage.
Calculate Cost of Goods Sold for the first time.
Record sales returns.
Determine gross sales.
A count checks the perpetual records and shows shrinkage (theft, damage, errors).
c5
When a buyer pays freight costs under FOB Shipping Point in a perpetual system, the buyer debits:
Inventory
Freight-Out
Delivery Expense
Cost of Goods Sold
Buyer pays freight under FOB shipping point; in a perpetual system it is part of inventory cost: Dr Inventory.
c5
Income from Operations is calculated as:
Gross Profit minus Operating Expenses
Net Sales minus Cost of Goods Sold
Gross Profit plus Other Revenues
Net Income plus Income Taxes
Income from operations = gross profit − operating expenses.
c5
Which account normally has a debit balance?
Sales Discounts
Sales Revenue
Purchase Discounts
Allowance for Doubtful Accounts
Sales Discounts is contra-revenue with a normal debit balance.
c5
Which of the following is a primary source of revenue for a merchandising company?
Sales revenue from selling merchandise inventory
Fees earned from consulting services
Interest revenue from bank deposits
Dividend revenue from equity investments
A merchandising company buys and sells tangible goods (merchandise inventory), earning Sales Revenue as its primary revenue source.
c5
Under a perpetual inventory system, what journal entry is recorded when a company purchases merchandise inventory on account for $4,200?
Debit Inventory $4,200; Credit Accounts Payable $4,200
Debit Purchases $4,200; Credit Accounts Payable $4,200
Debit Cost of Goods Sold $4,200; Credit Accounts Payable $4,200
Debit Inventory $4,200; Credit Cash $4,200
Under a perpetual inventory system, all purchases of merchandise directly increase (debit) the Inventory account.
c5
When goods are shipped **FOB Shipping Point**, which party holds legal title during transit and pays the freight charges?
Buyer holds title; Buyer pays freight
Seller holds title; Seller pays freight
Buyer holds title; Seller pays freight
Seller holds title; Buyer pays freight
Under FOB Shipping Point, ownership transfers to the buyer when the carrier picks up the goods at the shipping point, so the buyer owns the goods in transit and pays the freight (Freight-In).
c5
Under a perpetual inventory system, freight costs paid by the **buyer** to acquire merchandise are recorded as a debit to:
Inventory
Freight-Out
Delivery Expense
Cost of Goods Sold
Freight-in is a necessary cost to get inventory ready for sale, so under a perpetual system it is debited directly to Inventory.
c5
Freight costs incurred by the **seller** on outgoing merchandise sold under terms **FOB Destination** are classified as:
An Operating Expense (Freight-Out / Delivery Expense)
Inventory
Cost of Goods Sold
A Contra-Revenue account
Outbound freight paid by the seller (Freight-Out or Delivery Expense) is a selling expense reported under Operating Expenses on the income statement.
c5

A buyer purchases merchandise for $5,000 on account with credit terms of 2/10, n/30. If the buyer returns $500 of defective merchandise before paying, what is the amount of cash required to pay within the discount period?
Net payable after return = $5,000 - $500 = $4,500. The 2% discount on $4,500 is $90, leaving $4,500 - $90 = $4,410 in cash.
c5
Under a perpetual inventory system, how many journal entries are required to record a sale of merchandise on credit?
Two entries: one to record Sales Revenue and one to update Inventory and Cost of Goods Sold
One entry to record Sales Revenue
One entry to record Cost of Goods Sold
Two entries: one to record Accounts Receivable and one to record Cash
Every sale in a perpetual system requires two entries: (1) Dr. AR/Cash and Cr. Sales Revenue (at selling price), and (2) Dr. COGS and Cr. Inventory (at cost).
c5
What type of account is **Sales Returns and Allowances**, and what is its normal balance?
Contra-Revenue account; Debit balance
Expense account; Debit balance
Contra-Asset account; Credit balance
Liability account; Credit balance
Sales Returns and Allowances is a contra-revenue account deducted from Sales Revenue to determine Net Sales; therefore, it has a normal debit balance.
c5
A customer returns undamaged merchandise that was sold on account for $800 (cost $480). Under a perpetual system, what is the entry to record the return of the goods to inventory?
Debit Inventory $480; Credit Cost of Goods Sold $480
Debit Inventory $800; Credit Cost of Goods Sold $800
Debit Cost of Goods Sold $480; Credit Inventory $480
Debit Sales Returns and Allowances $480; Credit Inventory $480
Returned undamaged goods are placed back into Inventory at their cost ($480) and Cost of Goods Sold is reduced (credited) by $480.
c5
Which of the following items appears in the **Non-Operating Activities** section of a multiple-step income statement?
Interest Expense
Sales Discounts
Advertising Expense
Freight-Out
Interest Expense and Interest Revenue arise from financing/investing activities rather than primary merchandising operations, so they appear in the non-operating section.
c5
A company reports Sales Revenue of $250,000, Sales Returns and Allowances of $12,000, Sales Discounts of $8,000, and Cost of Goods Sold of $138,000. What is Gross Profit?
c5
If Net Sales are $400,000 and Gross Profit is $140,000, what is the company's Gross Profit Rate?
c5
Under a periodic inventory system, when a company takes a physical count at year-end and discovers inventory shrinkage (missing goods), how is it handled?
Automatically absorbed into Cost of Goods Sold
Debited directly to Loss on Inventory Shrinkage
Credited to Sales Revenue
Ignored until the next accounting period
Because periodic COGS is derived by subtracting Ending Inventory from Cost of Goods Available for Sale, any missing units lower Ending Inventory and automatically increase COGS.
c5
Credit terms of 1/15, EOM mean that a 1% discount is available if the invoice is paid:
Within 15 days after the end of the month in which the sale occurred
Within 15 days of the invoice date
By the 15th day of the current month
Within 1 day after the end of the month
EOM stands for End of Month, so 1/15, EOM grants a 1% discount if paid within the first 15 days of the following month.
c5
Which of the following accounts is closed to Income Summary with a **credit** during the closing process of a merchandiser?
Sales Discounts
Sales Revenue
Purchase Discounts
Interest Revenue
Sales Discounts has a normal debit balance, so it is closed with a credit (along with expense accounts) to Income Summary.
c5
A retailer buys goods for $3,000, terms FOB Shipping Point, and pays $150 freight. It returns $300 of goods and pays within the 2% discount period. What is the final cost of the inventory retained?
Net merchandise = $3,000 - $300 = $2,700. Less 2% discount ($54) = $2,646. Plus freight-in ($150) = $2,796.
c5
Which of the following best describes the operating cycle of a merchandising company compared to a service company?
Longer, because cash is first used to purchase inventory before selling and collecting receivables
Shorter, because inventory is sold for cash immediately
Identical in length and steps
Shorter, because merchandisers do not have accounts receivable
A merchandiser's operating cycle requires purchasing inventory first (Cash → Inventory → AR → Cash), making it longer than a service firm's cycle.
c5

Company X sold merchandise on account to Company Y for $12,000, terms 2/10, n/30, FOB Shipping Point. Company X prepaid $400 of freight charges on behalf of Company Y and added it to the invoice. Company Y returned $1,000 of goods and paid the balance within 10 days. How much cash did Company X receive?
Net merchandise = $12,000 - $1,000 = $11,000. The 2% discount applies ONLY to merchandise: $11,000 × 2% = $220. Cash received = ($11,000 - $220) + $400 freight = $11,180.
c5

Under a periodic inventory system, a company has Beginning Inventory $34,000, Purchases $190,000, Purchase Returns and Allowances $7,000, Purchase Discounts $3,000, Freight-In $8,000, and Ending Inventory $41,000. What is **Cost of Goods Purchased**?
c5
Using the data from the earlier problem, what is **Cost of Goods Sold**?
COGS = $34,000 (Beg. Inv.) + $188,000 (Cost of Goods Purchased) - $41,000 (End. Inv.) = $181,000.

Earlier problem: Under a periodic inventory system, a company has Beginning Inventory $34,000, Purchases $190,000, Purchase Returns and Allowances $7,000, Purchase Discounts $3,000, Freight-In $8,000, and Ending Inventory $41,000. What is **Cost of Goods Purchased**?
c5

At year-end, a perpetual inventory system shows an unadjusted Inventory ledger balance of $68,500. A physical inventory count reveals $66,900 of usable merchandise on hand. What adjusting journal entry is required?
Debit Cost of Goods Sold $1,600; Credit Inventory $1,600
Debit Inventory $1,600; Credit Cost of Goods Sold $1,600
Debit Sales Returns $1,600; Credit Inventory $1,600
No adjusting entry is required under a perpetual system
Inventory shrinkage of $68,500 - $66,900 = $1,600 is recorded by debiting Cost of Goods Sold and crediting Inventory.
c5

A company reports:
• Net Sales: $600,000
• Cost of Goods Sold: $372,000
• Selling Expenses: $95,000
• Administrative Expenses: $63,000
• Interest Revenue: $4,000
• Interest Expense: $11,000
What is **Income from Operations**?
Gross Profit = $600,000 - $372,000 = $228,000. Operating Expenses = $95,000 + $63,000 = $158,000. Income from Operations = $228,000 - $158,000 = $70,000. (Interest items are non-operating.)
c5
Using the data from the earlier problem, if the income tax rate is 20%, what is **Net Income**?

Earlier problem: A company reports:
• Net Sales: $600,000
• Cost of Goods Sold: $372,000
• Selling Expenses: $95,000
• Administrative Expenses: $63,000
• Interest Revenue: $4,000
• Interest Expense: $11,000
What is **Income from Operations**?
c5
Which of the following errors would cause **Gross Profit** to be **overstated** in the current period?
Recording Freight-In as Freight-Out (Delivery Expense)
Failing to record a purchase return on account
Overstating Sales Discounts
Recording a credit sale twice (both the sale and the cost entry)

Recording Freight-In as Freight-Out understates Cost of Goods Sold (increasing Gross Profit), while increasing Operating Expenses below Gross Profit (leaving Net Income unchanged, but overstating Gross Profit).
c5

A merchandiser purchases $9,000 of inventory on March 4, terms 3/10, n/30. On March 7, it returns $1,200 of goods. On March 14, it pays the balance due. Under a perpetual system, the March 14 entry includes a:
Credit to Inventory for $234
Credit to Inventory for $270
Credit to Purchase Discounts for $234
Debit to Inventory for $234
Balance owed = $9,000 - $1,200 = $7,800. March 14 is within 10 days (4 + 10 = 14). Discount = $7,800 × 3% = $234, which is credited to Inventory under a perpetual system.
c5
If a company's Gross Profit Rate increased from 38% last year to 42% this year, while Net Sales remained constant, which of the following is the most likely explanation?
Cost of Goods Sold as a percentage of Net Sales decreased from 62% to 58%
Operating expenses decreased significantly
Interest expense decreased
Income tax rates were lowered
Gross Profit Rate + COGS Rate = 100%. An increase in Gross Profit Rate from 38% to 42% directly means COGS fell from 62% to 58% of Net Sales.
c5

A customer returned damaged goods that originally sold for $600 (cost $360). The goods cannot be resold and have a scrap value of only $50. Under a perpetual inventory system, the entry to record the return of the merchandise is:
Debit Inventory $50; Credit Cost of Goods Sold $50
Debit Inventory $360; Credit Cost of Goods Sold $360
Debit Inventory $360; Credit Sales Returns and Allowances $360
Debit Inventory $600; Credit Sales Returns and Allowances $600
Damaged returned goods are debited to Inventory only for their estimated scrap/fair value ($50) and credited to COGS for $50.
c5
On a single-step income statement, how are revenues and expenses organized?
All revenues and gains are grouped together, and all expenses and losses are deducted in one step to arrive at Net Income
Gross Profit is calculated before Operating Expenses
Operating and Non-operating items are strictly separated
Cost of Goods Sold is shown as a contra-revenue account
A single-step income statement groups all revenues/gains together and deducts all expenses/losses in a single subtraction without reporting Gross Profit or Income from Operations.
c5
Under a periodic system, closing entries at year-end include:
Crediting Beginning Inventory and Debiting Ending Inventory
Debiting Beginning Inventory and Crediting Ending Inventory
Debiting Purchase Returns and Allowances and Crediting Inventory
Crediting Sales Revenue and Debiting Purchases
In periodic closing entries, Beginning Inventory (debit balance) is closed with a credit, and Ending Inventory (asset) is established with a debit.
c5
A company grants a customer a $450 **sales allowance** because merchandise shipped was slightly scratched; the customer keeps the goods. Under a perpetual system, what entry does the seller record?
Dr. Sales Returns and Allowances $450 / Cr. Accounts Receivable $450 (no inventory entry)
Dr. Sales Returns and Allowances $450 / Cr. Accounts Receivable $450 (and Dr. Inventory / Cr. COGS)
Dr. Sales Discounts $450 / Cr. Accounts Receivable $450
Dr. Allowance for Doubtful Accounts $450 / Cr. Accounts Receivable $450
Because the customer keeps the merchandise in a sales allowance, no goods are returned to inventory and no second entry is made.
c5
Which of the following accounts would appear on the **Balance Sheet** of a merchandising company?
Inventory
Freight-In
Freight-Out
Purchase Discounts
Inventory is a current asset reported on the Balance Sheet.
c5
If Net Sales are $850,000, Cost of Goods Sold is $510,000, and Net Income is $102,000, what are the company's **Profit Margin** and **Gross Profit Rate**?
Profit Margin 12.0%; Gross Profit Rate 40.0%
Profit Margin 20.0%; Gross Profit Rate 60.0%
Profit Margin 12.0%; Gross Profit Rate 60.0%
Profit Margin 40.0%; Gross Profit Rate 12.0%
c5
A retailer buys goods with a list price of $20,000 subject to a 15% **trade discount**, plus cash credit terms of 2/10, n/30. At what amount should the purchase initially be recorded?
Trade discounts are deducted immediately from list price before recording in the accounts: $20,000 × (1 - 0.15) = $17,000.
c5
Continuing from the earlier problem, if the retailer pays within 10 days, how much cash is paid?

Earlier problem: A retailer buys goods with a list price of $20,000 subject to a 15% **trade discount**, plus cash credit terms of 2/10, n/30. At what amount should the purchase initially be recorded?
c5
Which of the following is classified as a **Selling Expense** rather than an Administrative Expense?
Sales commissions and store advertising
Salary of the Chief Financial Officer (CFO)
Depreciation on corporate headquarters building
Legal and auditing fees
Sales commissions and store advertising are directly associated with making sales and delivering goods to customers (Selling Expenses).
c5
A company has Beginning Inventory of $50,000, Ending Inventory of $65,000, and Cost of Goods Sold of $310,000. What were **Net Purchases** during the period?
Net Purchases = COGS + End. Inv. - Beg. Inv. = $310,000 + $65,000 - $50,000 = $325,000.
c5
Why is a multiple-step income statement preferred by financial analysts over a single-step income statement?
It highlights key intermediate profitability measures like Gross Profit and Income from Operations
It produces a higher Net Income
It eliminates the need to report income taxes
It allows companies to omit non-operating losses
Distinguishing between Gross Profit, Operating Income, and Non-Operating items helps analysts evaluate core operating performance and margin trends.
c5

Company A sells merchandise on account to Company B for $15,000, terms 2/10, n/30, **FOB Destination**. Company A pays $600 to a trucking company for delivery. Company B returns $2,000 of goods and pays within 10 days. What is the **Net Sales** revenue recognized by Company A from this transaction?

Gross Sales ($15,000) - Sales Returns ($2,000) = $13,000. Sales Discount = $13,000 × 2% = $260. Net Sales = $13,000 - $260 = $12,740. (The $600 freight paid by Company A is Freight-Out, an operating expense, not a deduction from Net Sales.)
c5

Using the facts in the earlier problem, if the merchandise sold had a cost of $9,000 and the $2,000 returned goods had a cost of $1,200 (returned in salable condition), what is Company A's **Gross Profit** on this transaction?

Earlier problem: Company A sells merchandise on account to Company B for $15,000, terms 2/10, n/30, **FOB Destination**. Company A pays $600 to a trucking company for delivery. Company B returns $2,000 of goods and pays within 10 days. What is the **Net Sales** revenue recognized by Company A from this transaction?
c5

Under a **perpetual** inventory system, a buyer purchases $8,000 of goods, terms 2/10, n/30. The buyer pays **half** of the invoice ($4,000 gross) within the 10-day discount period, and pays the remaining $4,000 after 25 days. What is the total cash paid by the buyer?
The 2% discount applies only to the $4,000 portion paid within 10 days: $4,000 × 2% = $80 discount → $3,920 cash paid. The second $4,000 is paid in full. Total cash paid = $3,920 + $4,000 = $7,920.
c5

A merchandiser mistakenly recorded a $3,000 **sales return** from a customer as a **purchase return** (Dr. Accounts Payable $3,000 / Cr. Inventory $3,000) instead of Dr. Sales Returns and Allowances $3,000 / Cr. Accounts Receivable $3,000 (ignore cost entry). How does this affect the Trial Balance?
The Trial Balance will still balance, but Net Sales, Inventory, AR, and AP are all misstated
Total debits will exceed total credits by $6,000
Total credits will exceed total debits by $6,000
Net Income will be unaffected
Because equal debits ($3,000) and credits ($3,000) were posted, the trial balance still balances, even though four accounts are wrong.
c5
Which of the following combinations of changes would **definitely** cause a merchandiser's **Profit Margin** ((Net Income)/(Net Sales)) to **decrease**?
Gross Profit Rate decreases and Operating Expenses as a percentage of Net Sales increase
Gross Profit Rate increases and Operating Expenses decrease
Net Sales increase and COGS decreases
Interest Revenue increases and Income Tax Rate decreases
A lower Gross Profit Rate combined with higher Operating Expenses as a percentage of sales squeezes operating and net profit margins downward.
c5

A company operates in a jurisdiction with a 7% sales tax. It sells merchandise for $10,000 cash plus 7% sales tax (cost of goods $6,200). Under a perpetual system, what is the credit to **Sales Revenue**?
Sales taxes collected from customers are a liability (Sales Taxes Payable $700), not revenue. Sales Revenue is credited for $10,000.
c5

In a **periodic** inventory system, if a bookkeeper forgets to close the Purchase Discounts account (credit balance of $4,500) at year-end, what is the effect on **Net Income** and **Retained Earnings**?
Both are understated by $4,500
Both are overstated by $4,500
Net Income is unaffected; Retained Earnings is understated by $4,500
Trial Balance will not balance
Purchase Discounts reduces COGS. Failing to close its credit balance into Income Summary leaves COGS too high by $4,500, understating Net Income and Retained Earnings by $4,500.
c5
Which of the following items is deducted from **Sales Revenue** to arrive at **Net Sales**, rather than being classified as an Operating Expense?
Sales Discounts
Freight-Out
Sales Commissions
Bad Debt Expense
Sales Discounts and Sales Returns and Allowances are contra-revenue accounts deducted directly from Sales Revenue.
c5

Company P bought merchandise for $6,000, paid $300 Freight-In, returned $600 of goods, and received a 2% purchase discount. If Company P sold 80% of these goods for $7,500, what is its **Gross Profit**?
c5

A company uses a perpetual system and mistakenly records a **payment of $200 Freight-Out** as a debit to **Inventory** instead of Delivery Expense. If 100% of the company's inventory is sold before year-end, how are **Gross Profit** and **Net Income** affected?
Gross Profit is understated by $200; Net Income is unaffected (correct)
Gross Profit is understated by $200; Net Income is understated by $200
Both Gross Profit and Net Income are overstated by $200
Gross Profit is unaffected; Net Income is understated by $200
Because all inventory was sold, the $200 debited to Inventory flowed into COGS (understating Gross Profit by $200), while Operating Expenses were $200 lower. Thus, Net Income is unaffected.
c5
On a multiple-step income statement, where is a **Gain on Sale of Equipment** reported?
In the "Other Revenues and Gains" (Non-Operating) section
Added to Sales Revenue
Deducted from Cost of Goods Sold
Included in Gross Profit
Gains and losses from selling plant assets are peripheral to merchandising operations and are reported in the Non-Operating section.
c5
Which of the following statements regarding **periodic** vs. **perpetual** inventory systems is **FALSE**?
Perpetual systems eliminate the need to ever perform a physical inventory count
Perpetual systems provide better internal control over inventory quantities
Periodic systems require a physical inventory count to determine Cost of Goods Sold
Modern barcode scanners and POS terminals have made perpetual systems standard for most retailers
Perpetual systems still require an annual physical count to detect shrinkage, theft, and clerical errors.
c5

A buyer receives an invoice dated May 18 for $4,000, terms 2/10, n/30. On May 21, the buyer receives a $400 credit memo for returned goods. What is the **last day** to take the discount, and what is the discount amount?
June 17; $72
c5
If a merchandiser's **Operating Expenses** equal **Gross Profit**, and there are no non-operating items or taxes, what is the company's **Net Income**?
$0 (Break-even)
Equal to Net Sales
Equal to Cost of Goods Sold
Equal to Gross Profit
Net Income = Gross Profit - Operating Expenses = $0.
c5
Which of the following accounts will have a **zero balance** after closing entries are posted at year-end?
Sales Returns and Allowances
Inventory
Accounts Payable
Allowance for Doubtful Accounts
Sales Returns and Allowances is a temporary (nominal) contra-revenue account closed at year-end; the other three are permanent balance sheet accounts.
c5
Company S sells goods to Company B on December 29, terms FOB Destination. The goods arrive at Company B on January 3. When should Company S recognize Sales Revenue?
January 3
December 29
December 31
When Company B pays cash
Under FOB Destination, title and control transfer upon delivery to the buyer on January 3, so revenue is recognized on January 3.
c5
A company has Sales Revenue of $500,000, Sales Returns of $25,000, Gross Profit of $190,000, and Operating Expenses of $120,000. What is **Cost of Goods Sold**?
c5
Under a periodic system, what is the effect on **Cost of Goods Sold** if **Purchase Returns and Allowances** is understated by $2,500?
COGS is overstated by $2,500
COGS is understated by $2,500
COGS is unaffected
Net Sales is understated by $2,500
Purchase Returns and Allowances reduces Net Purchases and COGS; understating it causes Net Purchases and COGS to be overstated by $2,500.
c5
A retailer's Gross Profit Rate is 30% and its Operating Expenses are 22% of Net Sales. Assuming no non-operating items or taxes, what is its **Profit Margin**?
Profit Margin = 30% - 22% = 8%.
c5
Which of the following accounts is used by a merchandising company under a perpetual inventory system, but NOT by a service company?
Cost of Goods Sold
Accounts Receivable
